title: A hydrogen-like ion
hook: Change nuclear charge number and predict Bohr orbit radius.
misconception: Bohr orbit radius doubles when nuclear charge number doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply r_n = a₀n²/Z to compare Bohr orbit radius when nuclear charge number changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With the nonrelativistic Bohr model of a one-electron ion at fixed principal quantum number, r_n = a₀n²/Z. When nuclear charge number doubles, Bohr orbit radius becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model r_n = a₀n²/Z; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider the nonrelativistic Bohr model of a one-electron ion at fixed principal quantum number, with a nonzero initial result. If nuclear charge number triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on Bohr orbit radius?
recall.why: Apply r_n = a₀n²/Z under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
